learning: Iterations 5 to 7 show that wheel_radius raised progress when max_error held, mass 0.5 kg hurt, and track 0.14 m hurt. Speed is still the only geometry lever that has helped. If progress rises with max_error at or below 0.069, a further speed step is worth testing. If max_error rises above 0.069, speed has reached its useful limit and the next step is a controller change rather than more geometry.
notes: Adopts the Builder's wheel_radius 0.04 m step on the iteration 5 package. The controller is unchanged from iterations 5 and 7 so the speed effect is isolated. Max_error and steering_oscillation are the watch items, because higher ground speed can push the robot off the tape at bends.
rationale: The best race so far is iteration 5 (51.01): wheel_radius 0.035 m, mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m, sensors at x = -0.03 to 0.03 m with y = 0.04 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, and the iteration 4 gains (kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1). Iteration 5 raised s-bend progress from 0.150 to 0.155 with max_error held at 0.065. The two later attempts both lowered the score. Mass 0.5 kg (iteration 6) cut s-bend progress to 0.149 and raised max_error to 0.068. Track 0.14 m (iteration 7) cut s-bend progress to 0.145 and slalom progress to 0.100. Controller gain changes (iterations 0, 1, 4) left max_error essentially unchanged, and steering_oscillation has stayed between 0.07 and 0.16, so there is headroom. The Builder's intent is wheel_radius 0.04 m with everything else as in iteration 5. I take that geometry exactly and keep the iteration 5 controller unchanged, so the speed step is the only change and any shift in progress or max_error is attributable to it. I expect a higher ground speed to help progress only if max_error stays at or below about 0.069. Because the wheel is larger, the same PWM gives more ground speed, so drift at bends is the risk to watch.
